subject: NurtureMed: retention windows & prompt ephemerality — evidence request

From: Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@nurturemed.com>

Cc: NurtureMed Security <security@nurturemed.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 16:11:00 -0500
Subject: Retention windows & prompt ephemerality — evidence request

Marcus —

Hope you’re well. As part of our SCCs review and DPA update, our privacy team has a short set of follow-up questions about how Redwood handles transient data and logs for customer workloads. We’re filling out a SIG questionnaire and want to make sure the answers align with your operational controls and evidence. Could you confirm the following or point us to the supporting artifacts?

1) Operational logs (request/response traces): retention window, default and configurable values, and whether logs containing prompt text are retained by default.
2) Backups/snapshots of model state and system images: retention schedule, destruction workflow, and whether backups ever include user prompt content in any form.
3) Prompt ephemerality: does Redwood persist prompts beyond the inference request lifecycle for diagnostics or billing? If yes, retention periods and access controls.
4) Deletion/purge timelines: for account deletion or DPA erasure requests, what is the timeline to purge logs, backups, and cached prompting material?

If possible, we’d like PDF copies of any SOC 2 evidence excerpts, a short one-page summary of retention policies, and any related DPA language you rely on for these behaviours. We’re targeting a policy update by the end of month and would appreciate a 3 business-day turnaround if feasible.

Thanks — can loop in legal/security contacts on your side as needed.

Best,
Asha Pillai
DPO, NurtureMed

+1 617-555-0198

Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Draft responses & artifacts for NurtureMed (retention)

Marcus / Rishi —

Draft answers below (please review for technical accuracy and any additional nuance):

• Operational logs (request/response traces): Default retention is 30 days for structured operational logs (service/infra metrics); request-level access logs that may include metadata (no prompt bodies) are retained 90 days by default. Prompt text is not persisted to primary logs by default; prompts are only stored when customers enable debug/diagnostic logging or opt into usage telemetry.

• Backups/snapshots: Backups of system images and model artifacts are retained for 180 days by default in encrypted object storage. Backups do not include customer prompt text; model checkpoints are independent artifacts and do not contain request-level prompt data. Destruction workflow: scheduled lifecycle policies + cryptographic key rotation + deletion confirmation logs; retention reductions can be configured under Dedicated/Private engagements.

• Prompt ephemerality: Redwood treats prompts as ephemeral by default — prompts are processed in-memory and discarded after inference. For customers who enable debug-level logging or explicit prompt archiving features (opt-in), prompts are retained per customer-configured retention windows (documented and managed via the console).

• Deletion/purge timelines: For DPA erasure, we offer a 30–45 day window to purge request-level logs and cached prompt material when present; backups may extend this window. If prompt material is present in a backup snapshot, the timeline depends on the backup retention policy (typically up to 180 days) and we can apply targeted restores/expunges where feasible; for Dedicated/Private customers we provide tighter contractual SLAs.

Attached: redwood-log-retention-summary.pdf, redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf, redwood-backup-policy-excerpt.txt

Please advise any edits. Rishi, can you confirm the access-control language on who can retrieve archived prompts and whether we should tighten wording around "diagnostic access"?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the patience — attached are the documents we discussed and a short summary below. I’ve included the key points up front so your auditors can digest quickly.

Key points
- Default logging: system and infra logs 30 days; access/request metadata 90 days. Prompt text is not persisted in primary logs unless the customer enables diagnostic logging.
- Backups: model artifacts and system images retained 180 days by default; backups do not contain customer prompt text. Deletion of backups follows lifecycle policies plus secure deletion steps.
- Prompt ephemerality: prompts are ephemeral by design; opt-in features required to retain prompt text.
- DPA erasure: typical operational purge is 30–45 days for live logs/caches; backups may hold data per backup retention (up to 180 days). For Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate shorter contractual timelines.
